comment: Every build leg and stage that must have produced a build record before
anything is signed for provenance.
The completeness gate exists because the build matrix runs with
continue-on-error: true -- a leg can fail and the release still assemble,
which is fine for a nightly and NOT fine for a provenance claim. Signing
whatever happened to arrive would attest to a set nobody chose.
A leg is identified by os AND arch AND flavor. Architecture is part of
the key because it is the only thing that distinguishes some legs: two
runners can report the same os and flavour and produce binaries for
different machines.
Each stage lists artifact_patterns. Every pattern must be matched by at
least one artifact recorded at that stage, so a leg that quietly stops
producing its MSI fails here rather than shipping a release that is
missing one. Patterns are shell globs against the artifact's name.
Stages are separate statements about different bytes. macOS produces an
unsigned bundle in build-macos and a signed, notarized dmg in sign-macos;
codesigning REWRITES the file, so one digest cannot describe both and the
two are recorded apart.
Keep this in step with the `build` and `build-macos` matrices in
build.yml. The gate fails loudly when they disagree, which is the point.
